minutes.headline: Historical Commission unanimously voted to adopt tighter demolition delay bylaw amendments, including a daily fine.
minutes.summary: The commission met remotely, accepted amended February minutes, and spent much of the meeting on cemetery restoration (Goodrich Street and Arnold Lynch), the primary school and Brooks House, and a town survey binder found at the historical society. It voted unanimously to accept amendments to the demolition delay bylaw; the warrant has already closed, so the amendments would go to a fall town meeting.

what_happened.line: The Historical Commission voted unanimously by roll call to accept all the amendments to the demolition delay bylaw.
The amendments add a penalty per day, each day a separate violation, enforced by the building commissioner.
The spring warrant closed March 15, so the amendments wait for a fall town meeting; the chair will notify the planning board.
Cemetery work was discussed: stump grinding at Goodrich waits for the tree bill, and wall base work cannot happen before fall.
Members will meet separately at the historical society to review a town survey binder found there; the next meeting is April 22 at 7 pm.

why_it_matters: The change would give the town a stronger tool against demolishing old buildings without the delay review, but it takes effect only if a fall town meeting approves it.
Cemetery wall repairs are limited by the money left in the appropriation, so that work is pushed to fall.
watch_next: A fall town meeting warrant article on the demolition delay bylaw amendments.
The commission's next meeting, April 22, 2021 at 7 pm.
